messages:
jess: Hey — spotted weirdness in the cost dashboard: cache-savings are jumping between routes when a long session spans two slab windows. Not sure if it's routing or the windowing logic. Anyone seen this?

sam: yep saw this in staging yesterday. seems like we reassign prefetch credits at the window boundary which shifts savings.

miho: Is the dashboard using fixed slab windows (e.g. hourly) or sliding windows? I thought we moved to sliding for amortization.

jess: Dashboard is currently using fixed slabs by minute buckets. The econ service returns credits grouped by `billing_window_start`.

marta: That matches what I tested — when a session starts at :55 and goes past the hour, the prefetched tokens go to slab A then the hotpath tokens to slab B. Credits get split poorly.

luke: Quick thought: we could attribute cache savings to the session id instead of the time window until we close the session. But that changes the UI rollups/consistency for daily rollups.

miho: Right. Also chargebacks rely on deterministic windowed rollups for invoice stability. Switching to session-based could make numbers non-monotonic.

sam: Another option: keep fixed windows, but add a "session carryover" field in the API that annotates which slab got prefetched vs which got hit. Then dashboard can show 'attributed' vs 'observed' columns.

jess: That sounds promising. Minimal backend change and front-end option to toggle. UX would need a note about how credits are split.

marta: Sketch of SQL we used to compute current splits:
```sql
SELECT session_id, slab_start, SUM(prefetch_tokens) as prefetch, SUM(hit_tokens) as hits
FROM econ_prefetch_agg
WHERE timestamp >= :start AND timestamp < :end
GROUP BY session_id, slab_start;
```
This groups by slab_start which is the issue.

luke: If we instead group by `session_id` and then post-assign slab ownership heuristically, we can keep invoice windows intact. e.g. attribute prefetch credit to the slab where prefetch happened but tag hits to session owner slab until session closes.

miho: Need to check memory/compute impact — session grouping at query time could blow up for very large sessions. Might need a streaming aggregator or a sampling heuristic.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New econ-prefetch-schema migration will deploy in ~10m to staging. See <https://deploys.internal/redwood/1234> 

jess: OK — plan: (1) sam to prototype API change adding `carryover_tag` boolean, (2) miho to run perf estimate for session-group aggregation, (3) marta to mock UI column for attributed vs observed. We'll sync tomorrow. @sam @miho @marta

sam: on it. will post a short PR with proto API + example payload.

miho: I'll run a 7-day perf sim and post results to this thread.

marta: Will do a quick Figma mock and share in #design later today. :thumbsup:
